what_happened: In job 1ncn, the user corrected Athena's first reading of a request to encode the Project Olympus part of BRIEF.md as a file with a test and negative cases. The first reading covered the whole part. The previous attempt's verifier ran out of time. The user narrowed this job to sections 1 to 6 (vision, pantheon, feedback, the example, the two loops, R1 to R8). Sections 7 to 10, the governing philosophy and the 2026-10-17 addenda go to a second job. The file format, the test and its negative cases stay. The correction came before the work went on.
cause: Athena builds a reading from the request and its source document. Nothing makes it compare the reading's size with what one producer run and one verifier run can finish before their fixed deadlines. Nothing makes it split a sectioned document into one job per group of sections. It also does not use the earlier attempt's timeout as evidence that the scope was too big. A timed-out verifier on the prior attempt was a direct signal, but the new reading carried over the same scope. Only the user's correction applied the size bound. The reading was right about meaning, but too large for one job.
prevention: Add a size check at reading time. When the source is a numbered or sectioned document, the reading must list the sections it covers and the check must compare that count and length to a set bound for one producer run and one verifier run. If a prior attempt of the same request timed out in the producer or verifier, the check must require a smaller scope than that attempt, and the reading must split the remainder into named follow-up jobs. A reading over the bound is not accepted until it is narrowed.
proposed_request: Add a scope-size check to Athena's reading stage. When a request's source is a sectioned or numbered document, the accepted reading must name the sections it covers. Athena must compare that scope against a configured bound for one producer run and one verifier run, and must refuse or narrow readings that exceed it, listing the leftover sections as separate follow-up requests. When an earlier attempt of the same request ended in a producer or verifier deadline, the new reading must cover strictly less than that attempt did. Show it works with tests: (1) a reading over the bound is refused and split, (2) a retry after a verifier timeout gets a smaller scope, (3) a reading within the bound passes unchanged.
